_about: The dashboard To-Do feed. Refreshed at every Rule 8 checkpoint alongside the session handoff — this is the handoff distilled into plain language for the 📋 button on every tab. Split For Sam (curation / decisions only a human makes) and For Fable (engineering, the next session picks up).
_as_of: 2026-08-19 · Sky169 — repo posture and the auth model got measured and recommended; next up is the three new MAP Custom Reports.
_status: Two questions got answered this run, and both premises turned out to be partly wrong, which is where the value was. On the repos: two of the three are ALREADY out of Sam's personal account (they belong to the CPL-Initiative organisation) and CPLBrain was already private — so the real gap was that the organisation had only ONE owner. Sam has since made Pedro Campos an owner on the Supabase side. On going private: it would NOT make COBI private — on the free plan it takes the whole site dark, and on any paid plan below Enterprise the published site stays public either way. What private DOES hide is the half worth protecting: 555 methodology documents, 149 generators, Sierra's whole retrieval design. Sam's concern is proliferation, not privacy, and the licence already says All Rights Reserved. The recommended shape is a SPLIT — Sierra, the Fact Sheet, the veteran map and the landing pages stay public where they are; COBI and the methodology move to a private repo. Scope doc merged (#1242). On sign-in: magic links already cover more of COBI than the shared phrases do, so the recommendation is magic link plus ONE role field — not groups. The reviewer list went from 5 people to 10. Next session pivots to the three new MAP Custom Reports Sam has been waiting on.

items.text: Decide whether the public Knowledge Base stays CC BY 4.0 — its licence currently lets anyone remix our methodology commercially, which is the one thing working against what you asked for.
Check whether the CPL-Initiative GitHub organisation has a second OWNER. You added Pedro on Supabase, but GitHub is where the website, the 29 scheduled jobs and the 8 secrets live.
Look at the billing page and tell us if GitHub is on Free or Team — the private-repo step cannot start on Free without taking the site down.
Say go (or not) on the sign-in change: magic link plus one role per person, no groups. Nothing goes dark during the switch.
Ask Pedro for the three viewName values and column lists for the new Custom Reports — that is all we need, and it is much less work for him than the automation he offered.
Confirm nobody is stranded by the GR phrase change — anyone who holds ONLY the GR phrase now needs the shared team phrase too.
Tell the four new people they can now sign in with a magic link from the About menu instead of typing a shared phrase.
Fetch the three new MAP Custom Reports and compare them against Supabase. First establish whether they are on the API we already use, or only in the report builder.
Treat the comparison as a reconciliation, not a load — where the new extract disagrees with Supabase, it is probably our stale copy resolving, and that needs confirming rather than fixing.
Work out what Catalog Year unlocks — it is the one genuinely new field, and it lets an articulation be pinned to the catalog it was approved under.
When Sam gives the go: add the role column to the reviewer list, leaving all 132 existing permission rules untouched.
Move Sierra and the veteran map to their own public repo — zero risk, no decisions attached, and it proves the split works before the harder half.
